title: Intertwined magnetoresistance and Hall multifunctionality in a non-coplanar magnetic Weyl semimetal DyB4
authors: Long Chen, Yulin Shen, Songxue Chi, Seunghoon Song, Yang Zhang, Jian Liu, Haidong Zhou
abstract: Anomalous magneto-transport responses provide complementary probes of orbital motion, momentum-space topology, and real-space spin chirality, yet their integration into a single material remains rare because their underlying requirements often compete. A promising materials-design strategy is to realize a magnetic Weyl semimetal that combines linearly dispersive high-mobility bands with tunable non-coplanar magnetism while limiting spin-dependent scattering. Here we identify DyB4, a frustrated rare-earth tetraboride, as a magnetic Weyl semimetal candidate that embodies this strategy and hosts intertwined magnetoresistance and Hall multifunctionality. Neutron diffraction reveals a sequence of field-tunable magnetic states, including non-coplanar spin configurations and PT-symmetry-broken phases. First-principles calculations identify steep linear dispersions and field-induced Weyl points near the Fermi level. Magneto-transport measurements establish a rare fourfold combination of extremely large magnetoresistance, chiral-anomaly-like negative magnetoresistance, large anomalous Hall conductivity arising from cooperative intrinsic Berry curvature and skew scattering, and scalar-spin-chirality-driven topological Hall responses. This multifunctionality arises from the distinct yet weakly coupled roles of itinerant carriers and localized 4f moments, which enable high-mobility transport, field-induced Weyl topology, and non-coplanar magnetism. DyB4 therefore provides a 4f-electron platform for correlating orbital transport, momentum-space Berry curvature, and real-space spin chirality, suggesting a route toward multifunctional magnetic topological materials.
summary: This work investigates DyB4 as a multifunctional magnetic Weyl semimetal capable of hosting multiple anomalous transport responses simultaneously. By combining neutron diffraction with advanced magnetotransport measurements and theoretical calculations, the authors demonstrate that tunable non-coplanar magnetism facilitates the coexistence of large magnetoresistance, AHE, and topological Hall effects. This suggests a promising route for designing next-generation magnetic topological materials.
main_problem: The research aims to identify a single material platform that can simultaneously exhibit and correlate multiple anomalous magneto-transport responses (magnetoresistance, AHE, topological Hall effect) by integrating orbital motion, momentum-space topology, and real-space spin chirality.
main_result: DyB4 is identified as a rare magnetic Weyl semimetal exhibiting a fourfold combination of large magnetoresistance, chiral-anomaly-like negative magnetoresistance, anomalous Hall conductivity, and topological Hall responses.
method: The study combines neutron diffraction to map field-tunable magnetic states with first-principles calculations (for electronic structure) and detailed magneto-transport measurements (MR, AHE, THE).
model_or_system: The physical system is DyB4, a frustrated rare-earth tetraboride proposed as a magnetic Weyl semimetal. Its functionality relies on the weak coupling between itinerant conduction electrons ($	ext{Dy-}4d/	ext{B-}2p$) and localized $4f$ moments ($	ext{Dy-}4f$).
key_observables: Extremely large magnetoresistance (XMR), anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{Axy}$), topological Hall resistivity ($ho_{Txy}$), and evidence of non-coplanar spin chirality ($\chi_{ijk}$).
important_parameters: Field-tunable magnetic states, including Non-Coplanar Antiferromagnetic (NCAFM) and Ferromagnetic (NCFM) phases; the Fermi level proximity to Weyl points.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on multi-carrier modeling for Hall resistivity and assumes that the observed phenomena are governed by the interplay between orbital motion, Berry curvature, and spin chirality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the classification of materials with coexisting anomalous responses (Fig 1), $	ext{H-T}$ phase diagrams showing magnetic transitions (Fig 2), electronic band structures revealing Weyl points (Fig 3), and transport measurements demonstrating XMR/NMR coexistence across different magnetic phases (Figs 4, 5, 6).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical motivation by classifying materials exhibiting coexisting anomalous responses. It then presents experimental evidence using neutron diffraction to map field-tunable non-coplanar magnetic states in DyB4. Finally, it correlates these magnetic structures with transport measurements and electronic structure calculations to demonstrate the fourfold multifunctionality.
why_interesting: The explicit connection drawn between localized $4f$ magnetism (rare-earth elements) and topological band features (Weyl semimetals) provides a concrete platform for studying emergent quantum phenomena driven by spin-orbit coupling and magnetic order, which is highly relevant to modern condensed matter theory.
